description: Every quote snapshot in one journey, oldest first, in the get_quotes shape. A journey is a collection of quote snapshots, all saved with one `journey_reference`, that build up to a complete sold (bound) journey; it is complete when its latest quote is `sold`. Returns `{ journey_reference, start_date, end_date, quote_count, limit, offset, has_more, quotes: [{ quote_reference, project_reference, project_name, version_reference, version, created_at, status, valid, result, indicator, journey_reference, exec_time_ms, error, amended_result, amended_valid, sold, quoted_by, source, quote_url }], journey_url, next_steps }`. `quoted_by` (`{ user_reference, email, role }`, or null) is who ran each quote — each stage can be completed by someone different (a person, an AI agent, an integration) — and `source` how (api | mcp). `actions` is the journey's history from the actions table, oldest first: `[{ type (quoted | price_changed | validity_changed | sold | unsold), quote_reference, created_at, by: { email, role }, via (api | mcp | dashboard), from, to, note }]` — who completed each stage and who re-priced or bound it. The last quote is where the case stands now (`sold` true means the journey is complete); compare `result` and `valid` from one quote to the next to explain what changed, and call get_quote with a quote_reference for one quote's full review (inputs, rules that fired, how the result was reached). Paged with `limit` (default and max 100) and `offset`. A journey_reference with no quotes is a tool error.

journey_reference.description: The journey's journey_reference (exact match), from get_journeys or a quote's journey_reference.

limit.description: Optional. Page size, default and max 100.

offset.description: Optional. Quotes to skip from the start of the journey, for paging.
